outputs.L1: Provided are: a starter generator including a field portion having a permanent magnet, and an armature unit including first and second multi-phase windings arranged in parallel; a first power conversion unit including a first positive-side DC terminal connected to a battery and a plurality of first AC terminals connected to the first multi-phase winding, the first power conversion unit being configured to bidirectionally convert power between DC and AC; a second power conversion unit including a plurality of second AC terminals connected to the second multi-phase winding, the second power conversion unit being configured to control current input and output via the second AC terminals; and a control unit configured to detect a positional relationship between the field portion and the armature unit based on an output voltage of the second multi-phase winding, and to control the first power conversion unit and the second power conversion unit in accordance with the detected positional relationship.
outputs.L2: The system includes a starter generator with a field section that uses a permanent magnet, and an armature assembly having first and second multi-phase windings arranged in parallel. It also includes a first power conversion unit with a first positive-side DC terminal connected to a battery and multiple first AC terminals connected to the first multi-phase winding. This first power conversion unit is configured to perform bidirectional conversion between direct-current power and alternating-current power. A second power conversion unit is also provided, having multiple second AC terminals connected to the second multi-phase winding and configured to regulate current input and output through those second AC terminals. outputs.L3:
The starter generator includes a field portion provided with a permanent magnet and an armature unit having first and second multi-phase windings. The first and second multi-phase windings are arranged in parallel with one another so that they can operate in association with the same field portion while being connected to separate power conversion units.

A first power conversion unit is electrically connected to a battery through a positive-side DC terminal. The first power conversion unit is also connected to the first multi-phase winding through a plurality of AC terminals corresponding to the respective phases of the winding. This first power conversion unit is configured to perform bidirectional power conversion between direct-current power and alternating-current power. Accordingly, it can convert DC power supplied from the battery into multi-phase AC power for driving the starter generator as a motor, and it can also convert AC power generated by the first multi-phase winding into DC power for charging the battery or supplying electrical loads.

A second power conversion unit is connected to the second multi-phase winding through its own plurality of AC terminals. The second power conversion unit controls the current input to and output from the second multi-phase winding via these AC terminals. In this way, the second power conversion unit can regulate the electrical state of the second multi-phase winding independently of, or in coordination with, the first power conversion unit.

A control unit is provided to control operation of both the first and second power conversion units. The control unit detects the positional relationship between the field portion and the armature unit on the basis of the output voltage generated by the second multi-phase winding. Using this detected positional relationship, the control unit controls the switching or power conversion operation of the first power conversion unit and the second power conversion unit. As a result, the starter generator can be appropriately controlled during both starting operation, in which electrical power is supplied to generate torque, and power generation operation, in which mechanical rotation is converted into electrical power.
outputs.L4:
A starter generator system is configured to operate both as an electric starter motor and as an electric generator. The system includes a rotor having a permanent-magnet field and an armature provided with first and second multi-phase armature windings arranged in parallel. The first and second armature windings are connected to respective power conversion units, each of which is capable of bidirectional power conversion and current control. As a result, electrical power can be supplied to the armature windings during a starting operation, and generated electrical power can be delivered from the armature windings during a generating operation.

The system further includes a control unit that controls the operation of the power conversion units. In particular, the control unit detects the relative rotational position between the rotor and the armature based on an output voltage produced by the second multi-phase armature winding. This detected position information is used to coordinate the switching and current control of both the first and second power conversion units. By deriving rotor-position information from the voltage of one of the existing armature windings, the system can control commutation and power conversion accurately without requiring a separate rotor-position sensor.

This arrangement improves the operation of the starter generator by reducing the number of components, simplifying the overall structure, and improving reliability. Because the position detection is performed using the second armature winding, the system can maintain appropriate phase control of the power conversion units during starting and generating modes. The coordinated control of the two power conversion units also enables efficient use of the parallel armature windings, allowing the starter generator to provide high starting torque and stable generated output while avoiding the added cost, space, and complexity associated with a dedicated position-detection device.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an electric starter generator system with dual multi-phase armature windings, a battery-connected bidirectional inverter, a second current-control converter, and rotor position detection from the second winding voltage.
counterfactuals.output: An electric starter-generator system includes a dynamoelectric machine having a rotor and a stator provided with first and second multi-phase armature windings. A bidirectional inverter is coupled between a battery and the first multi-phase armature winding for supplying starting current to the machine in a motor mode and for delivering generated electrical power to the battery in a generating mode. A second converter is coupled to the second multi-phase armature winding and is controlled to regulate current in the second winding independently of the bidirectional inverter. A controller operates the inverter and the second converter to control torque and generated output of the machine. Rotor position is determined from a voltage induced in, or appearing at, the second multi-phase armature winding, and the determined rotor position is used for commutation or phase control of at least one of the inverter and the second converter. The arrangement enables starter and generator operation with improved control accuracy, reduced need for separate rotor position sensors, and independent management of current in the dual armature windings.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into formal patent language: a starter generator includes a PM field, two multiphase windings in parallel, a first inverter connected to a battery, a second converter connected to the second winding, and a controller using induced voltage in the second winding for position detection and converter control.
counterfactuals.output:
A starter-generator system comprising:

a permanent magnet electric machine including a rotor having a permanent magnet field and a stator having a plurality of multiphase stator windings, the plurality of multiphase stator windings including a first multiphase winding and a second multiphase winding arranged in parallel with one another;

a first power converter electrically coupled to the first multiphase winding and configured to exchange electrical power with an energy storage device;

a second power converter electrically coupled to the second multiphase winding and configured to exchange electrical power with the second multiphase winding; and

a controller operatively coupled to the first power converter and the second power converter,

wherein the controller is configured to determine a rotor position of the permanent magnet electric machine based at least in part on an induced voltage generated in the second multiphase winding, and to control operation of the second power converter in response to the determined rotor position.

In some embodiments, the energy storage device comprises a battery, and the first power converter comprises an inverter configured to supply alternating current to the first multiphase winding during a starting mode and to rectify or otherwise process electrical power generated by the permanent magnet electric machine during a generating mode.

In some embodiments, the second power converter is configured to selectively energize the second multiphase winding to produce torque in cooperation with the first multiphase winding. The controller may be configured to sense back electromotive force induced in the second multiphase winding by rotation of the rotor and to use the sensed back electromotive force as a position feedback signal for commutation, phase advance, or other control of the second power converter.

In some embodiments, the first and second multiphase windings are electrically isolated from one another while being magnetically coupled through the stator and rotor of the permanent magnet electric machine. The controller may be further configured to control the first power converter and the second power converter independently or cooperatively to provide starter operation, generator operation, or combined starter-generator operation.

An electrical starter-generator apparatus comprising a permanent magnet field machine having first and second parallel multiphase stator winding sets, a first inverter coupled between a battery and the first winding set, a second converter coupled to the second winding set, and a controller configured to derive rotor position information from voltage induced in the second winding set and to regulate the second converter according to the derived rotor position information.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Japanese-patent-translation-style description of a motor generator apparatus where one multiphase winding is driven by a bidirectional DC/AC power converter and another winding is used by a second converter to sense rotor/armature positional relationship via output voltage.
counterfactuals.output:
A motor generator apparatus includes a rotary electric machine having a stator, a rotor disposed so as to be rotatable relative to the stator, a first multiphase armature winding, and a second multiphase armature winding. The first multiphase armature winding and the second multiphase armature winding are provided so as to have a predetermined electrical phase relationship with respect to a magnetic pole position of the rotor.

A first power converter is connected to the first multiphase armature winding. The first power converter is constituted by a bidirectional DC/AC power converter capable of performing power conversion between a DC power source and the first multiphase armature winding. The first power converter supplies multiphase alternating-current power to the first multiphase armature winding during a motor operation of the rotary electric machine, and rectifies or regenerates alternating-current power generated in the first multiphase armature winding to the DC side during a generator operation of the rotary electric machine.

A second power converter is connected to the second multiphase armature winding. The second power converter is configured to detect an output voltage generated in the second multiphase armature winding. The output voltage of the second multiphase armature winding varies in accordance with a positional relationship between the rotor and the armature winding. Accordingly, the second power converter obtains position information indicative of a relative position between the magnetic pole of the rotor and the stator armature by using the output voltage of the second multiphase armature winding.

In one embodiment, the second power converter includes voltage detecting means for detecting phase voltages or line-to-line voltages of the second multiphase armature winding, and position estimating means for estimating a rotor position or an electrical angle based on the detected voltage. The detected output voltage may be an induced voltage generated in accordance with rotation of the rotor, or may be a voltage component generated in response to a high-frequency signal applied to the second multiphase armature winding. The second power converter supplies the obtained position information to a control unit.

The control unit controls switching operation of the first power converter on the basis of the position information obtained from the second power converter. Thus, current supplied to the first multiphase armature winding is controlled in synchronism with the rotor position. As a result, torque generation and power generation can be appropriately controlled without requiring a separate mechanical position sensor.

The first multiphase armature winding and the second multiphase armature winding may be electrically insulated from each other and may be accommodated in common slots of the stator or in mutually different slots of the stator. The first multiphase armature winding is mainly used for torque generation and power generation, whereas the second multiphase armature winding is mainly used for detection of the relative positional relationship between the rotor and the armature. Therefore, even when a large drive current flows through the first multiphase armature winding, the second multiphase armature winding can provide a voltage signal suitable for position detection.

According to the motor generator apparatus described above, one multiphase winding is driven by the bidirectional DC/AC power converter, and another multiphase winding is used by the second converter for sensing the rotor/armature positional relationship based on output voltage. Therefore, a compact and reliable motor generator apparatus can be provided, in which drive control and generator control are performed with high accuracy while reducing the need for an independent rotor position sensor.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
